title: Asian financial crisis
summary: On 2 July 1997 the Bank of Thailand announced a float of the baht after reserves fell to $2,850 million, against $38,700 million in 1996. The devaluation began a deep financial crisis across much of East Asia: Malaysia, the Philippines and Indonesia let their currencies weaken, and the South Korean won fell from 886 to 1,701 per dollar between 2 July and 31 December 1997.

uncertainty.note: Start is the day of the baht float. End year follows the CRS report title (1997-98); the crisis had no single end date on the pages opened.

as_recorded.value: On July 2, 1997, Thailand devalued its currency relative to the U.S. dollar.
on 2 July 1997, the BOT announced the float of the Thai Baht

importance.justification: A regional currency and banking crisis that spread across East Asia and triggered IMF programmes.

reviewer_note: Least sure of the pin: the sources say Thailand, and the pin is Bangkok on the assumption that the central bank announcement was made there, which no opened page states. The Bank of Thailand calls it a float and the CRS timeline a managed float; the summary says float. The reserve figures are the Bank of Thailand's; the CRS report cites a different foreign exchange figure ($33 billion).
